title: TidalMesh: Topology-Driven AllReduce Collective Communication for Mesh Topology
problem: Existing AllReduce algorithms are topology-aware adaptations of generic algorithms (ring, tree) to physical 2D mesh networks, resulting in a mismatch between logical and physical communication patterns that wastes bandwidth and increases latency.
motivation: AllReduce is a critical collective operation for both DNN training and inference at scale, and 2D mesh interconnects are widely deployed in scale-out ML systems, yet no algorithm is specifically designed from the ground up to exploit 2D mesh topology characteristics.
method: TidalMesh is a topology-driven AllReduce algorithm designed natively for 2D mesh networks. It pushes data flows between endpoint nodes in a wave-like (tidal) pattern that aligns with the mesh grid structure, fully utilizing bidirectional links and minimizing congestion. Sparse TidalMesh minimizes the bandwidth overhead of the base algorithm. Collective communication unrolling enables software pipelining by superimposing different AllReduce phases (ReduceScatter, AllGather) so that compute and communication overlap across multiple concurrent AllReduce operations, effectively hiding collective communication latency.
key_novelty: A topology-driven AllReduce algorithm designed natively for 2D mesh interconnects that pushes tidal flows between endpoint nodes to achieve near-optimal bandwidth utilization, rather than adapting topology-agnostic ring/tree algorithms.
contributions: TidalMesh AllReduce algorithm natively designed for 2D mesh topology achieving near-optimal bandwidth utilization
Sparse TidalMesh variant that reduces bandwidth overhead while maintaining performance
Collective communication unrolling technique enabling software pipelining of AllReduce phases on 2D mesh
Up to 24% AllReduce performance improvement over state-of-the-art on a 64-node 8x8 2D mesh

metrics.speedup: up to 24% AllReduce performance improvement on 64-node 8x8 2D mesh

baselines: state-of-the-art AllReduce algorithms (ring-based and topology-aware variants)
limitations: TidalMesh is specifically designed for 2D mesh topologies; its applicability to other topologies (torus, fat-tree, dragonfly) requires separate investigation.
primary_theme: topology-native AllReduce algorithm for 2D mesh scale-out interconnects
